title: Abdominal hernias: recognizing problems and choosing care
intro: An abdominal hernia occurs when tissue pushes through a weakness in the abdominal wall. A groin, navel or previous surgical scar may bulge. Different hernia types have different risks, so the same advice cannot fit every lump.

sections.heading: Understanding the problem
paragraphs: A bulge may become more visible on standing or coughing and reduce when lying down. Pain or dragging can occur, but not every lump is a hernia; persistent or changing swelling needs examination.

sections.heading: Assessment and tests
paragraphs: A clinician examines the location and symptoms; imaging is used if findings are unclear. Explain previous surgery, bowel symptoms and pregnancy. A groin lump in a woman needs particular assessment because femoral hernias can be overlooked. Bring your medicine list and previous results; ask which findings would change the plan.

sections.heading: Treatment choices
paragraphs: Surgery repairs the defect; method and mesh choice depend on the hernia. Observation may suit selected minimally symptomatic cases after advice, but is not appropriate for every type. Discuss recurrence, chronic pain and recovery. Agree how benefit and adverse effects will be checked before changing treatment.

sections.heading: Everyday care
paragraphs: Manage constipation and persistent cough with advice and adapt painful lifting. Support garments may relieve symptoms but do not close the defect. Do not repeatedly force a painful lump back into place. Choose a routine you can maintain, and discuss barriers such as cost, work or language.

sections.heading: Follow-up and warning signs
paragraphs: A suddenly painful, firm or non-reducible bulge, vomiting, abdominal swelling or inability to pass stool or gas may mean obstruction or strangulation. Seek emergency assessment rather than waiting for a routine surgery appointment.

examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira discusses a small uncomplicated hernia and receives a monitoring plan that specifies which changes require urgent help.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben’s bulge becomes very painful with vomiting. He seeks emergency care instead of using a support belt or pushing harder on the lump.
